title: Vinyl Plank vs Tile in Bathrooms: Cost, Comfort and Durability
meta: Vinyl plank or tile in a Kirkland bathroom? LVP installs for $2.50 per sq ft in labor and feels warmer; tile wins in wet rooms. Wills Flooring compares both.
keywords: vinyl plank vs tile bathroom, LVP in bathroom Kirkland, is vinyl plank good for bathrooms, tile vs luxury vinyl plank cost, bathroom flooring Kirkland WA

blocks.lead: For most Kirkland bathrooms, vinyl plank is the better everyday choice: it installs for $2.50 per sq ft in labor at Wills Flooring, feels warmer and quieter underfoot, and handles splashes and steam without trouble. Tile still wins in true wet rooms, around curbless showers, and in a primary bath where resale buyers expect it.
blocks.detail: The honest split is comfort and cost on one side, permanence and prestige on the other. Below we compare the two on price, feel, water, durability and what Kirkland buyers actually notice.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives in a Kirkland remodel like this: the hall bath in a 1980s Rose Hill split-level has cracked 4x4 tile, the kids' bath in a Juanita two-story has peeling sheet vinyl, and the homeowner wants to know whether to go back with tile or use the same vinyl plank that is going on the main floor. Both are legitimate. The right answer depends on which bathroom, who uses it, and how long you plan to stay. Here is how we walk through it at a free in-home estimate.

blocks.text: Cost: what each one really costs to put in

items.title: Vinyl plank labor: $2.50 per sq ft
items.text: That is Wills Flooring's installation labor for click-lock or glue-down LVP. Material is separate and quoted from the samples we bring. The 500 sq ft minimum means a 60 sq ft bathroom is best bundled with the hallway, laundry or main floor.

items.title: Tile labor: several times higher
items.text: Tile is set one piece at a time over a prepared, waterproofed substrate, then grouted and sealed. National averages for tile installation labor typically run three to five times LVP labor per square foot, and we quote tile on site rather than publishing a rate.

items.title: Prep is where tile pulls ahead in cost
items.text: Tile needs a stiff, flat, waterproofed base: backer board or an uncoupling membrane, thinset, and often floor leveling. LVP wants a flat subfloor too, but a thin underlayment and a clean surface are usually enough.

items.title: Time on the job
items.text: A tiled bathroom floor is two to three days with cure time between setting and grouting. The same bathroom in vinyl plank is done in a morning, and you can use it that evening.

blocks.note: Tile figures are national averages for comparison only, not Wills Flooring prices. See our published price list for what we do publish.

blocks.text: Water and durability: the honest comparison

a.title: Holds up well when
items: The bathroom has a tub or a curbed shower, not a walk-in wet room
Water on the floor is splashes and steam, wiped up within a day
The subfloor is dry and flat and the perimeter is sealed with silicone
You choose a rigid-core plank with a 20 mil or thicker wear layer

b.title: Is the safer choice when
items: The shower is curbless or the whole floor is a wet zone
A steam shower or soaking tub keeps the room humid for hours
You want a 40-year floor and will never redo the room
It is the primary bath in a home you will sell to Eastside buyers

blocks.html: Quality vinyl plank is waterproof through the plank, but the floor system is only as good as its edges. Water that runs under a click-lock floor at an unsealed tub flange sits on the subfloor. Tile with proper waterproofing underneath protects the subfloor itself. That is why the shower type matters more than the material name.

items.title: Primary bath: tile still expected
items.text: In Houghton, Bridle Trails and along the lake, buyers touring a primary suite expect tile or stone on the floor and in the shower. A vinyl plank primary bath in a home listed near the top of the neighborhood reads as unfinished to that buyer.

items.title: Kids' and hall baths: LVP is fine
items.text: Nobody marks down a Totem Lake or Finn Hill home because the kids' bathroom has a good-looking vinyl plank floor. Warm, quiet and matching the hallway reads as thoughtful, not cheap.

items.title: Condos and townhomes
items.text: Juanita and downtown Kirkland condos often have sound rules and slab floors. LVP with an acoustic underlayment satisfies most HOAs faster than tile, which may need a sound-rated membrane approved by the board.

items.title: Continuity sells
items.text: A single vinyl plank floor running from the hallway through the powder room with no threshold is one of the most common requests we get from Kirkland remodelers, and it photographs well.

blocks.text: Mistakes that make vinyl plank fail in a bathroom

items.html: Skipping the silicone. The perimeter at the tub, shower curb and toilet flange has to be sealed. A floating floor with an open gap at the tub is the number one cause of a swollen subfloor.
Installing over old cushioned sheet vinyl. Soft, embossed or curling vinyl telegraphs through and lets planks flex at the joints. It comes up, or gets a skim coat, first.
Ignoring the toilet. The flange has to sit at the right height on the new floor. Raising the floor by a quarter inch without a flange extender means a wax ring that never seals.
Choosing a thin, flexible plank. Bathrooms swing in temperature and humidity every day. A rigid SPC core with a 20 mil wear layer moves far less than a 4 mm flexible plank.
Not checking the subfloor first. A soft spot near the toilet in a 1970s Kirkland bath means old water damage. We probe it at the estimate and replace the plywood before anything goes down.

blocks.text: How to decide in five minutes

items.text: Curbless or steam: tile. Tub or curbed shower: either.
Primary bath in a high-value Kirkland home: lean tile. Hall, kids' or basement bath: LVP is the smarter spend.
If you want a warm floor without paying for radiant heat and an electrician, that is LVP.
Need the only bathroom back tomorrow: LVP. Can lose it for three days: either.
Doing the main floor in vinyl plank anyway: run it through the hall bath and powder room and let the 500 sq ft minimum cover it.
items.note: Example: 640 sq ft main floor + 45 sq ft bath = 685 × $2.50 = $1,713 labor

faq.q: Is vinyl plank a good idea in a bathroom?
faq.a: Yes, in a bathroom with a tub or a curbed shower. Rigid-core vinyl plank does not absorb water, is warm and quiet, and installs in a morning. The perimeter must be sealed with silicone, and we do not recommend it in curbless wet rooms or steam showers.

faq.q: How much does it cost to put vinyl plank in a bathroom in Kirkland?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's labor is $2.50 per sq ft with a 500 sq ft minimum, so a bathroom on its own would be billed at the minimum. Most customers bundle the bathroom with a hallway or main floor. Material, removal and prep are quoted at the free estimate.

faq.q: Is tile more durable than vinyl plank?
faq.a: Tile lasts longer, often 40 years or more, and shrugs off standing water when it is waterproofed underneath. But tile cracks if the subfloor flexes and chips when something heavy drops. Quality vinyl plank lasts 15 to 25 years in a bathroom and is easier to repair.

faq.q: Does vinyl plank in the bathroom hurt resale value?
faq.a: In a hall or kids' bath, no. In the primary bath of a higher-priced Kirkland home, buyers expect tile and may notice. If you are selling within a few years, we usually suggest tile in the primary and vinyl plank everywhere else.

faq.q: Can I put vinyl plank over my existing bathroom tile?
faq.a: Often yes, if the tile is flat, solidly bonded and the grout lines are shallow. Wide or deep grout joints get skim-coated first so they do not telegraph through. We check bond and flatness at the estimate and tell you if the tile needs to come out.

faq.q: Will a heated floor work under vinyl plank?
faq.a: Many rigid-core planks are rated for radiant heat up to a manufacturer limit, usually around 80 to 85 degrees at the surface. Tile handles heat better and transfers it faster. If a warm floor is the main goal, tile with radiant mats is the classic setup.
